newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says its troops will not leave Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says its troops will not leave Sierra Leone.

text.p: Nigeria is not contemplating pulling out its troops from Sierra Leone, a senior Nigerian army general said on Wednesday.
Nigerian troops dominate a West African force stationed in Sierra Leone with the stated aim of reversing a May coup there by junior army officers.

"If we pull out that will be a defeatist attitude," Major-General Patrick Aziza told reporters while answering their questions after a meeting of Nigeria's all-military Provisional Ruling Council in the capital Abuja.

"We have been holding consultations with the men in command there and we hope it will yield positive results," said Aziza, the commander of the Lagos Garrison Organisation of the army. He did not elaborate.
A senior Nigerian official said earlier West African foreign ministers would meet in Conakry, Guinea on Thursday to discuss the May coup and ways of dealing with it.
Nigerian foreign minister Tom Ikimi left the Nigerian capital of Abuja on Tuesday to hold consultations with some of his counterparts in the sub-region before the Conakry meeting, the official said.
"The meeting will work out the ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) framework for dealing with the Sierra Leone issue," he added.
The regional force massed in Sierra Leone is seeking to reinstate the elected president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, who was overthrown on May 25.
But the widely expected military action to remove the soldiers who toppled Kabbah has failed to materialise.

Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on June 2 but Nigerian soldiers were in turn attacked by Sierra Leone forces and their Revolutionary United Front (RUF) rebel allies at a hotel where the Nigerians were guarding foreigners.
Further Nigerian military intervention is beginning to look unlikely after Ghana, one of Nigeria's closest allies in the region, opted for diplomatic means to resolve the Sierra Leone debacle.

On Tuesday, Sierra Leone's military rulers called for an all-party consultative conference in which a timetable for fresh elections would be discussed, saying this would bring together the army, Kabbah, the RUF rebels and the Kamajor civil militia.
